rationale: Across published cohorts of patients with biallelic GTF3C3 variants (OMIM #621201), simplified gyral pattern (HP:0009879) is documented in only a small minority of cases. In the initial gene-discovery series by Abdel-Hamid et al. (2025), only 1 of 4 assessed individuals (25%) exhibited a moderate-to-severe simplified gyral pattern, while predominant neuroimaging findings were cerebellar hypoplasia/atrophy, frontal lobe hypoplasia, and corpus callosum defects. Additional cohorts (e.g., De Hayr et al., 2025, describing 12 individuals across 7 families) similarly emphasize cerebellar and corpus callosum malformations as the characteristic radiological findings, with cortical simplification noted as an infrequent, severe-end manifestation. A systematic review by Chapleau et al. (2026) confirmed that simplified gyral pattern has been documented in only an isolated patient in the literature, keeping the aggregate frequency well below the 30% threshold.

evidence.text: Brain imaging of four individuals from three unrelated families showed brain atrophy with predominant cerebellar involvement and frontal lobe hypoplasia, with moderate-to-severe simplified gyral pattern present in only one patient (1/4; 25%).

new_directions.question_text: Does the presence of simplified gyral pattern correlate specifically with biallelic null/truncating variants or severe missplicing alleles versus hypomorphic missense variants in GTF3C3?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying the genotype-phenotype correlation would establish whether simplified gyral pattern is restricted to near-complete loss-of-function variants, aiding prognostic counseling.

new_directions.question_text: What are the exact comparative frequencies of corpus callosum hypoplasia versus cerebellar vermis hypoplasia across all international registry cases of GTF3C3?
new_directions.rationale: Identifying the single most sensitive neuroimaging hallmark (cerebellar vs callosal anomalies) will provide clinicians with definitive screening criteria to differentiate GTF3C3 from other POLR3/TFIIIC-related disorders.
